subject.title: Exec provider: 1Password op CLI spawns daemon processes, hangs on macOS Tahoe (needs --cache=false)

question: Should OpenClaw handle the 1Password CLI cache-daemon problem as documentation/doctor guidance only, or add generic exec-provider behavior that can disable cache-like side effects without hardcoding `op` in core?
rationale: Root policy keeps core lean and avoids owner-specific behavior in core, but the report affects secret-provider startup, security, and macOS Gateway service reliability.

options.title: Docs and doctor guidance
options.body: Document `--cache=false` or `OP_CACHE=false` for 1Password exec providers and add diagnostic guidance without changing runtime command behavior.

options.title: Generic exec safety option
options.body: Design a non-1Password-specific exec-provider option or plugin integration contract for disabling cache/daemon side effects, with upgrade-safe docs and tests.

options.title: Runtime auto-detection
options.body: Inject `OP_CACHE=false` or prepend `--cache=false` when the command is `op`, accepting a core special case for this third-party CLI.

recommendation.title: Docs and doctor guidance
recommendation.body: Document `--cache=false` or `OP_CACHE=false` for 1Password exec providers and add diagnostic guidance without changing runtime command behavior.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete has the strongest recent current-checkout ownership signal for the affected secrets docs/runtime surface.
